extracted.intended_audience: applicants, IP practitioners, businesses and government officials involved in industrial property registration and enforcement in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements from the Vietnamese law on industrial property governing registration, examination, publication, rights, infringements, and procedures for inventions, designs, marks, layout-designs, geographical indications and business secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation on use of collective marks — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation on use of collective marks consists of the following principal contents: a/ Name, address, grounds of establishment and operations of the collective organization being the owner of the mark; b/ Criteria for becoming a member of the collective organization; c/ List of organizations and individuals permitted to use the mark; d/ Conditions for use of the mark; e/ Measures for handling acts violating the regulation on use of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies mandatory items that a collective-mark usage regulation must include (ownership/organization details, membership criteria, permitted users, usage conditions, enforcement measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation on use of certification marks — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation on use of certification marks consists of the following principal contents: a/ The organization or individual being the mark owner; b/ Conditions for using the mark; c/ Characteristics of goods or services certified by the mark; d/ Methods of evaluating characteristics of goods or services and methods of controlling the use of the mark; e/ Expenses to be paid by the mark user for the certification and protection of the mark, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out required elements for certification-mark regulations including owner identity, use conditions, certified characteristics, evaluation and control methods, and user fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication registration application — identifying documents and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents, samples and information identifying a geographical indication registered for protection include: a/ The name or sign being the geographical indication; b/ The product bearing the geographical indication; c/ The description of peculiar characteristics and quality, or reputation of the product ... (description of peculiar characteristics); d/ The map of the geographical area bearing the geographical indication; e/ Documents evidencing that the geographical indication is under protection in the country of origin in case of a foreign geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must supply identifier (name/sign), product, detailed description of characteristics/reputation, geographic map, and proof of protection in country of origin for foreign GIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of peculiar characteristics for geographical indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of peculiar characteristics must include: a/ Description of microbiological and perceptible properties of the relevant product, including raw materials, and physical, chemical, ... ; b/ Method of identification of the geographical area bearing the geographical indication; c/ Evidence proving that the product originates from such geographical area (Article 79 meaning); d/ Description of local and stable methods of production and processing; e/ Information on relationship between the peculiar characteristics and quality, or reputation of the product and the geographical conditions; f/ Information on the mechanism of self-control of the peculiar characteristics or quality of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires both scientific/technical description and proof linking product qualities/reputation to the geographic area plus governance/self-control mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — required contents for authorized representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must have the following principal contents: a/ Full name and address of the principal and the attorney; b/ Scope of authorization; c/ Valid term of authorization; d/ Date of making the power of attorney; e/ Signature and seal (if any) of the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization for IP-related procedures must be written as a power of attorney including identity, scope, term, date and signature/seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney validity when no term specified
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney without any valid term shall be considered indefinitely valid and shall have its validity terminated only when the principal so declares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an explicit term renders the POA indefinite until principal revokes in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum documents and information required for receipt of industrial property applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial property registration application shall only be received if it consists of at least: a/ A declaration for registration (sufficient info to identify applicant and sample of mark/list of goods or services for marks); b/ A description including scope of protection for inventions; photos/drawings and description for industrial designs; description of peculiar characteristics for GIs; c/ Voucher of payment of filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative receipt requires identity/declaration, the substantive description appropriate to the IP type, and proof of filing fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date shall be the date on which the application is received by the concerned state management agency or the international filing date in case of applications filed under international treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date ties to receipt by the agency (or international filing date), important for priority and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property registration applications shall be subject to formal examination for evaluating their validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal examination checks presence/format and basic eligibility before substantive steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — invalidity ground: failure to fulfill formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if it does not fulfill the formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes missing documents, improper forms, or other administrative defects; triggers intended refusal and opportunity to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — invalidity ground: subject matter ineligible for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if the subject matter stated in the application is ineligible for protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal exam can detect ineligible subject matter (e.g., excluded categories); such invalidity leads to refusal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — invalidity ground: applicant lacks registration right
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if the applicant does not have the registration right, including where registration right belongs to more than one persons but one or several do not agree with the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership/entitlement defects (co-owners not consenting, wrong claimant) can render an application invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — invalidity ground: contravention of filing mode
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if it is filed in contravention of regulations on the filing mode provided for in Article 89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant filing procedures (e.g., wrong channel, missed formality) are grounds for rejecting receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination — invalidity ground: failure to pay fees and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if the applicant fails to pay fees and charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpayment at filing is a formal ground for not accepting an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures where application is invalid (notice and correction cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications in invalid cases the agency shall: a/ Issue notice of intended refusal to accept, clearly stating reasons and setting time limit to correct errors or object; b/ Issue notice of refusal to accept if applicant fails to correct or objects unjustifiably; c/ Issue notice of refusal to accept registered semiconductor layout-design certificate if applicable; d/ Carry out procedures for granting if applicant properly corrects or makes justifiable objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal-process includes opportunity to correct/contest; agency must state reasons and time limits; proper corrections lead to acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and further processing when no invalidity found
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications not falling into invalid cases the agency shall issue notices of acceptance of valid applications or carry out procedures for granting protection titles and registering them in the national register of industrial property (layout-design special rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once accepted, the application proceeds to publication, substantive examination (if applicable), and possible grant/registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of accepted industrial property applications — general rule and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted applications shall be published in the Official Gazette of Industrial Property. Invention applications are published in the 19th month from filing or priority date (or earlier at applicant request). Industrial design, mark or geographical indication applications shall be published within 2 months from acceptance. Layout-designs are published by direct access at the agency with reproduction restricted; principal information published within 2 months from grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different IP types have distinct publication schedules; layout-designs have confidentiality/access limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality before publication for inventions and industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publication the state agency shall keep confidential information in invention and industrial design applications. Disclosure by cadres/public employees leads to discipline and compensation if damage results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-publication confidentiality is mandated and enforced; wrongful disclosure carries penalties and compensation liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party opinions during pendency — form and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: From publication of an application until prior to the decision on grant, any third party may express opinions to the agency on grant or refusal; such opinions must be in writing and be accompanied by documents or quote the source of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables public input/observations but requires written evidence or source citation; applies up to decision issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination — time limits and consequence of non-request
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 42 months after the filing date or priority date an applicant or third party may request substantive examination (fee payable). For invention applications requesting utility solution patents the limit is 36 months. If no request is filed within the time limit the application is considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination is not automatic for inventions — requires timely request and fee; failure leads to deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications are subject to substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination is applied to: a/ Invention registration applications accepted as valid and with requests for substantive examination; b/ Industrial design, mark or geographical indication registration applications accepted as valid. Layout-design registration applications shall not be substantively examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which IP types receive substantive evaluation and the exception for layout-designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rights to amend, supplement, divide, change or convert applications before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Before agency notifies refusal or decides to grant, applicant has rights to: a/ Amend or supplement; b/ Divide the application; c/ Request recording of changes in name/address; d/ Request recording of change of applicant due to transfer/bequest/inheritance or decision; e/ Convert invention application between invention patent and utility solution patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may modify filings prior to final decision; conversion between patent types is allowed under rules; fees apply for these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for amendment/division/conversion procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters for completion of procedures specified (amendment, division, conversion, etc.) shall have to pay fees and charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative costs apply to post-filing procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on scope/nature change by amendment or supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment or supplement must not expand the scope of the subject matter already disclosed or change the nature of the subject matter stated in the application and must ensure the uniformity of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are constrained to the originally disclosed matter (no added matter; no change in nature); uniformity must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for divided applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of division of an application, the filing date of the divided application shall be determined to be the filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division retains the original filing date for priority purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of applications — procedure and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Before decision or refusal the applicant may withdraw the application in writing personally or through representation (POA must authorize withdrawal). From declaration of withdrawal all further procedures stop; fees for procedures not yet commenced may be refunded on request. Withdrawn invention/design applications before publication and withdrawn mark applications are considered never filed, except where they serve as grounds for claims for priority right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal halts processing and may allow refunds; withdrawal may still preserve priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusal to grant protection titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant shall be refused if: a/ There are grounds to affirm the subject matter does not fully satisfy protection conditions; b/ The application satisfies conditions but is not earliest filing/priority date as per Article 90; c/ The application falls into a case of Article 90(2) but lacks consensus of all applicants. For layout-designs, grant is refused if they do not fulfill formal requirements in Article 109.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal can be on substantive inadequacy, priority/lateness, co-applicant consent issues, or formal defects for layout-designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures on intended refusal to grant and consequences of objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where refusal cases appear the agency shall: a/ Notify an intended refusal clearly stating reasons and setting time limit for objection; b/ Notify refusal if no objection or unjustifiable objection; c/ Grant protection and record it if applicant makes a justifiable objection. If an objection appears to an intended grant, the application shall be re-examined regarding the matters objected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must provide reasons and time to object; justifiable objections can reverse intended refusals or trigger re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting and entry into national register
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application does not fall into refusal cases and the applicant has paid fees, the agency shall decide to grant a protection title and enter it in the national register of industrial property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant contingent on absence of refusal grounds and payment of required fees; results in registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for processing — form and substantive examinations and re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Form examination within one month from filing. Substantive examination time limits: inventions — 12 months from date of publication (or from receipt of request if filed after publication); industrial design, mark or GI — 6 months from publication. Re-examination time limit equals two thirds of initial examination time, may be prolonged in complicated cases but must not exceed initial examination time. Duration for amendment or supplementation is not counted into these time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines statutory processing deadlines and that applicant amendment periods pause the clock.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed under treaties to which Vietnam is a contracting party are collective referred to as international applications. International applications and their processing shall comply with relevant treaties. The Government will guide implementation of treaty provisions in compliance with the principles laid down in this Chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International filings follow treaty rules and implementing government guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owners of industrial property objects — general definitions and GI ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of inventions, industrial designs or layout-designs mean organizations or individuals granted protection titles. Owners of marks mean those granted protection titles or having internationally registered marks or well-known marks. Owners of trade names mean organizations or individuals lawfully using such trade names in business. Owners of business secrets mean lawful acquirers who keep them secret. The owner of Vietnam's geographical indications is the State; the State grants the right to use GIs to organizations/individuals that produce goods bearing such GIs and may exercise or grant management rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines ownership categories and notes GI national ownership with state-managed rights-of-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors of inventions/designs/layout-designs — definitions and moral/economic rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are persons who personally created the industrial property objects; co-authors exist for joint creation. Moral rights include: a/ To be named as authors in patents/certificates; b/ To be acknowledged as authors in documents where inventions/designs/layout-designs are published or introduced. Economic rights are rights to receive remunerations as provided in Article 135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates moral/personal attribution rights from economic remuneration; applies to creators irrespective of ownership arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic rights of owners of industrial property objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners shall have economic rights: a/ To use or authorize others to use industrial property objects; b/ To prevent others from using industrial property objects (per Article 125); c/ To dispose of industrial property objects (per Chapter X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core proprietary rights: exploitation, exclusion, and disposition/licensing/transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an invention — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an invention means: a/ Manufacturing the protected product; b/ Applying the protected process; c/ Exploiting utilities of the protected product or product manufactured under the protected process; d/ Circulating, advertising, offering, stocking for circulation the product; e/ Importing the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a broad set of acts that constitute 'use' for enforcement and infringement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an industrial design — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an industrial design means: a/ Manufacturing products with appearance embodying the protected design; b/ Circulating, advertising, offering and stocking such products; c/ Importing such products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar exploitation and commercialization acts define use for designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a layout-design — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a layout-design means: a/ Reproducing the layout-design; manufacturing semiconductor integrated circuits under the protected layout-design; b/ Selling, leasing, advertising, offering or stocking copies of the protected layout-design, semiconductor integrated circuits manufactured under it or articles containing such circuits; c/ Importing copies of the protected layout-design or circuits/articles containing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates reproduction, manufacture and commercial acts constituting use for layout-designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a business secret — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a business secret means: a/ Applying the business secret to manufacture products, provide services or trade in goods; b/ Selling, advertising for sale, stocking for sale or importing products manufactured with the application of the business secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial application and distribution of goods/services derived from secret information constitute use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a mark — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a mark means: a/ Affixing the protected mark on goods, goods packages, means of business, means of service provision, transaction documents in business activities; b/ Circulating, offering, advertising or stocking for sale goods bearing the protected mark; c/ Importing goods or services bearing the protected mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers marking, commercialization and importation as uses of marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a trade name — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a trade name means performing acts for commercial purposes by using it to name oneself in business activities, expressing it in transaction documents, signboards, products, goods packages and means of service provision or advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying and presenting a business under the trade name in commerce constitutes use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a geographical indication — acts constituting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a geographical indication means: a/ Affixing the protected GI on goods or goods packages, means of business and transaction documents in business activities; b/ Circulating, offering, advertising for sale or stocking for sale goods bearing the protected GI; c/ Importing goods bearing the protected GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines GI use analogous to marks for labeling and commercial acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prevent others from using industrial property objects — scope and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners and those granted rights may prevent others from using IP unless use falls into specified exceptions. Exceptions include: a/ Using inventions/designs/layouts for personal/non-commercial purposes or for evaluation, analysis, research, teaching, testing, trial production or information collection for license procedures; b/ Circulating, importing, exploiting utilities of products lawfully put on the market (including overseas), except products put on overseas markets not by owners/licensees; c/ Using inventions/designs/layouts solely for maintaining operation of foreign means of transport in transit or temporarily staying in Vietnam; d/ Using inventions/designs by persons with prior use right per Article 134; e/ Using inventions authorized by competent state agencies per Articles 145 and 146; f/ Using layout-designs without knowing/proving obligation to know they are protected; g/ Using marks identical/similar to protected geographical indications where such marks acquired protection in an honest manner before GI filing date; h/ Using in an honest manner people's names, descriptive marks of type/quantity/quality/utility/value/geographical origin and other properties of goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner's exclusion right is broad but limited by public-interest, prior use, honest practice and non-commercial/research uses; specific exceptions listed must be checked case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to right to prevent others regarding business secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of business secrets shall not have the right to prevent others from: a/ Disclosing or using business secrets acquired without knowing or obligation to know they were unlawfully acquired; b/ Disclosing secret data to protect the public; c/ Using secret data specified in Article 128 not for commercial purposes; d/ Disclosing or using business secrets obtained independently; e/ Disclosing or using business secrets obtained by analyzing/evaluating lawfully distributed products, unless otherwise agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates lawful paths to acquire/use information that defeat a business-secret claim (independent discovery, legitimate public-interest disclosure, reverse engineering etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts infringing inventions, industrial designs and layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts are regarded as infringements: 1. Using protected inventions or protected industrial designs or industrial designs insignificantly different from protected ones, or protected layout-designs or any original part thereof within valid terms without permission; 2. Using inventions/designs/layouts without paying compensations according to provisional rights (Article 131).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement covers unauthorized use and use without provisional-rights compensation; 'insignificantly different' standard applies for designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts infringing business secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts regarded as infringements include: a/ Accessing/acquiring business-secret information by acts against secret-keeping measures; b/ Disclosing or using business secrets without permission; c/ Breaching secret-keeping contracts or deceiving/inducing/buying off/forcing/seducing/abusing trust to access/acquire/disclose secrets; d/ Accessing/acquiring business secrets of applicants for licenses by acts against secret-keeping measures; e/ Using or disclosing business secrets while knowing or obligated to know they were unlawfully acquired; f/ Failing to perform secret-keeping obligations. Lawful controllers of secrets include owners, lawful licensees and managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers a broad set of wrongful acquisition and misuse acts; includes contractual and tortious bases for liability and identifies lawful controllers entitled to protect secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to keep test data secret and non-use period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where law requires applicants for licenses for trading pharmaceuticals or agro-chemical products to supply test results or other data that are business secrets and applicants request secrecy, the competent licensing agency must apply measures so such data are neither used for unhealthy commercial purposes nor disclosed, except when disclosure is necessary to protect public. From submission until end of a 5-year period from date licenses are granted, that agency must not grant licenses to subsequent applicants in whose applications the said secret data are used without consent of submitters, except specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a 5-year regulatory data protection period for certain test data, subject to public-protection exceptions; agencies must protect confidentiality and limit reliance by competitors without consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts infringing marks, trade names and geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringing acts for marks include: a/ Using signs identical with protected marks for identical goods/services on registered lists; b/ Using identical signs for similar/related goods/services if likely to cause confusion; c/ Using signs similar to protected marks for identical/similar/related goods/services if likely to cause confusion; d/ Using signs identical with or similar to well-known marks (including translations/transcriptions) for any goods/services if likely to cause confusion or misleading impression about relationship with well-known mark owners. Infringement of trade names includes using commercial indications identical/similar to others' trade names that cause confusion. For GIs: a/ Using GI for products not satisfying GI criteria though originating from the area; b/ Using GI for similar products to take advantage of reputation; c/ Using signs identical/similar to protected GIs for products not originating from the area and misleading consumers; d/ Using protected GIs of wines/spirits for products not from the area even if true origin is indicated or words like 'imitation' appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out confusion/misleading tests for marks and trade names and special stringent rules for wines/spirits GIs; 'likely to cause confusion' and reputation-take advantage are central standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts regarded as unfair competition include: a/ Using commercial indications to cause confusion as to business entities, activities or commercial origin; b/ Using commercial indications to cause confusion as to origin, production method, utilities, quality, quantity or other characteristics of goods/services; c/ Using marks protected in a treaty country where representatives/agents are prohibited from using such marks without consent or justification; d/ Registering/possessing/using domain names identical with or confusingly similar to protected trade names or marks or GIs without right, for purpose of possessing domain names, benefiting from or prejudicing reputation/popularity of such marks, trade names or GIs. Commercial indications include marks, trade names, symbols, slogans, GIs, package/label designs. Acts include affixing such indications, selling, advertising, stocking and importing goods with such indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers deceptive practices, misuse of domain names, false origin representations and other acts that exploit or mislead about commercial identity or product qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights for applicants prior to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant knows their invention or industrial design is being commercially used by another without prior use right, the applicant may notify in writing the user of the filing, specifying filing date and publication date so that the user shall terminate or continue such use. For layout-designs commercially exploited by the person with registration right or licensee before grant, if aware of another's commercial use, they may notify the user of their registration right to terminate or continue use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows applicants to assert provisional interests before grant by notifying alleged infringers; may underpin later compensation claims per Article 131 and provisional rights rules.
